$comment: Authoritative attestation reference for the production publicai-gateway CVM. Fetched at runtime by the /proof page. composeHash was read back from the CVM's RTMR3 event log on 2026-09-01 and cross-checked against the Phala control-plane API; both report 66dccbaa. Image digests are the linux/amd64 children of the cosign-signed proof-v24 index for sub2api (INDEX 694f165c) built by publish-tee-images run 33492070309 from commit 255111212; the attestor image is deliberately left at its proof-v20 pin (INDEX cef1d03d) because deploy/attestor was not touched, and repinning it would widen the attested surface for nothing. VERIFICATION SCOPE, stated plainly: composeHash, osImageHash, the image digests and the build commit were each read back from a live source, and composeHash was cross-checked against two independent ones. The cosign keyless signature was NOT verified locally for this release - the workflow performs the signing and its run succeeded, and anyone can verify certificate identity https://github.com/FiiLabs/sub2api/.github/workflows/publish-tee-images.yml@refs/heads/feat/two-sided-market plus the embedded githubWorkflowSha against the sourceCommit below, but this file does not claim it was done. This release carries no backend or migration change at all - git diff against the previously deployed commit b6f903328 is empty under backend/, so what shipped is a copy change and nothing else. It brings the public pricing copy into line with the parameters actually in the database: consumers are billed at 14 percent of official API list pricing (group rate_multiplier 0.14 on both the shared-supply and fallback groups, changed from 0.22), and providers receive 50 percent of what the platform collects (share_ratio 0.50, changed from 0.80). Both numbers had to move together. The two figures appear on the same page, so shipping one without the other produces a page that contradicts itself - billing at 14 percent of list while promising the provider 80 percent of the charge reads as though the platform pays out more than it keeps, and the providers who actually do that arithmetic are the ones worth keeping. The changed surfaces are the landing page hero stat, the provider-facing revenue-share block in both the Chinese and English locales, and the documentation site at docs.apex1.us, which is a separate repository and was updated in the same pass. One test assertion had to be relaxed rather than satisfied: the landing-page guard forbade the bare string 50 percent, which existed to catch a stale half-price claim from an earlier pricing scheme. Fifty percent is now the correct value of a different quantity, so the guard was narrowed to price-shaped phrasings only. The same page now carries two instances of 50 percent that mean opposite things - what we charge versus what we pay out - and that is recorded in the test comment. Earlier in this line: proof-v23 (alert minimum sample size, SLA error definition), v22 (attach-time probe, abuse alerts made visible), v21 (supplier self-service re-authorization), v20 (supply concurrency 3->15), v19 (abuse detection, shipped disabled), v18, v17, v16/v15. osImageHash, appId and instanceId are unchanged; the deploy passed --no-dev-os explicitly, because phala deploy silently switches to a dev OS image when it detects a local SSH key and a dev OS would void the attestation, and the control plane confirms is_dev false after the rollout. A full postgres backup was taken and verified beforehand - downloaded from S3, gzip-tested, 108 COPY sections. This rollout completed in 86 seconds with no incident.
